Maria Alvarez: quick heads-up — after the 02:12 canary deploy we observed a ~22% drop in KV prefix cache hit-rate on cluster-gpu-b during an autoscale spike. tail latency nudged up too.
DeployBot: deploy finished: service=runtime-gpu, version=2026.03.18-canary-14, time=2026-03-18T02:12:07Z
Maria Alvarez: pasted a tiny profile excerpt below (see lines for batching and seeding). looks like batching window shortened and our seeder keying is very high-cardinality.
--- PROFILE EXCERPT ---
batch_window_ms: 10 (previously 25)
batcher_coalesce_rate: 0.62
seed_keying: exact_prefix_text
prefix_seed_latency_ms_p95: 12.4
cache_hit_rate_prefix_p1m: 0.58 -> 0.45
--- end excerpt ---
Oliver Chen: no kernel/quantization changes in this canary? those would change per-token times and could reshape batching behavior.
Maria Alvarez: confirmed no kernel swaps. The main change was dynamic batching window tuned from 25ms -> 10ms to reduce latency, but it reduced coalescing: fewer requests in the same batch so warmers often miss prefixes that would've been seeded earlier.
Lee Park: right — our warmers seed keys by exact prompt text. with high prefix variability and shorter windows, coverage collapses. we should move to normalized keying with len buckets.
Anika Bose: proposal: change seeder key to normalized prefix + len_bucket + model_family. also add a cooperative assignment so we don't double-seed the same clusters across pods.
Lee Park: coop design sketch — deterministic partitioning + claim-with-ttl to avoid duplication. idea:
- reservoir sample prefixes from live traffic (5m window)
- normalize and cluster (similarity threshold 0.8)
- hash cluster -> assigned pod via (hash % pod_count)
- pod attempts CAS on claim key `kv-seed-assign:{model_family}:{cluster_hash}` with TTL, if success it seeds cluster entries at a rate-limit
This reduces wasted seeds and evictions.
Oliver Chen: add metrics: `seed_overlap` (duplicate seeds across pods), `unique_key_cardinality`, `evicted_count`. Also capture `kernel_selected` histogram so we can spot indirect effects.
Maria Alvarez: experiment plan (feature-flagged): four arms for 48h: A = cooperative normalized seeder (handshake), B = synthetic-high-entropy exact seeder (current), C = light seeding (low rate), D = control (no warmers). compare per-prefix hit-rate, p99/p99.9 latency, memory pressure, evictions.
Anika Bose: dashboard metrics to wire:
- prefix_hit_rate (1m / 5m) per model
- unique_prefix_keys by cluster
- cache_evictions/sec
- seed_success_rate and seed_latency_p95
- p99 and p99.9 generation latency
- seed_overlap (should approach 0 for coop)
Oliver Chen: acceptance criteria: if coop sees +15% prefix_hit_rate and >5% p99 improvement with no >30% jump in evictions or memory, promote. rollback if mem pressure or evictions spike too much.
Maria Alvarez: sample coop config (behind FF):
```
coop_seeder_mode: handshake
reservoir_window_seconds: 300
similarity_threshold: 0.8
max_seed_rate_per_pod: 2000/s
keying: [prefix_norm,len_bucket,model_family]
circuit_breaker: max_seeds_per_min: 30000, backoff_ms: 500
claim_ttl_seconds: 60
```
Lee Park: will implement CAS via `kv-seed-assign:{model_family}:{cluster_hash}` using the cluster hash and pod_id. each pod claims only its assigned clusters and renews TTL while seeding. keep claim TTL short to allow rebalance during scale events.
Anika Bose: we'll also implement a decaying-weight sampler so recent prefixes get higher priority but long-tail prefixes still get occasional seeds. helps keep freshness without starving tail.
Maria Alvarez: roll-out checklist:
- feature flag + canary smoke run (coop enabled but not actually seeding)
- enable coop on cluster A, synthetic on B, light on C, control on D
- collect 48h, auto-generate comparison report and diff dashboard
- alerts: `coop-seed: prefix_hit_rate drop >10% over 15m` (pager)
